acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — A workspace package @personal-events/s3-repository (at packages/s3-repository/) exposes a bin entry point named event-push that accepts: --type (alert | notification, required), --priority (integer 1–8, required), --source (required), --name (required), --payload <path|-> (optional; - reads stdin), --work-item <url> (optional), --bucket <name> (optional), --timestamp <iso> (optional), and --dry-run (optional).

verification.command: node packages/s3-repository/dist/main.js --type alert --priority 5 --source cron --name backup-failed --bucket x --dry-run
verification.definingInputProperty: The built bin invoked with the full documented flag set
verification.assertions: Exit 0; every listed flag is accepted; the resolved key is printed

acceptanceCriteria.explicitUserApproval: Package name @personal-events/s3-repository with bin event-push approved by user 2026-08-31, superseding the prior @personal-events/event-push wording.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — The package provides the live implementation of the EventRepository Context.Tag defined by @personal-events/core (AWE-153), as an Effect Layer. Its put returns Effect<PutOutcome, EventWriteError> exactly as the contract declares. The CLI is a consumer of that layer, not a parallel code path — AWE-155 and AWE-162 obtain the identical put by providing the same layer.

verification.definingInputProperty: The Layer typed against core's exported Context.Tag rather than a locally redeclared interface
verification.assertions: S3EventRepositoryLayer type-checks as Layer<EventRepository>; put's signature is Effect<PutOutcome, EventWriteError>
The tag is imported from core, not redefined locally — counterexample against a parallel contract

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — The assembled event validates against the @personal-events/event-model schema before any network call is attempted, with acknowledged and handled defaulting to false. A validation failure performs zero S3 requests.

verification.definingInputProperty: An invalid event combined with a bucket value that would fail loudly if contacted
verification.assertions: Exit 2 with a validation message; the injected S3 client's call count is exactly 0; acknowledged and handled default to false on the valid path

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — The object key is produced exclusively by the event-model codec (buildKey). No key string is assembled anywhere in this package, and the field schemas Priority, NoDotString and IsoInstant are imported from event-model, never re-declared.

verification.definingInputProperty: The package source, searched for re-declared field-schema bounds
verification.assertions: Neither the 1–8 priority bound nor the no-dot pattern is re-declared — the specific contract-forking failure the feature calls out

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — Round-trip parity is proven by test: for a matrix of inputs — including source and name values containing dots, and boundary priorities 1 and 8 — the key produced by buildKey parses back through parseKey to identical components.

verification.definingInputProperty: Inputs actually carrying dots in source/name and the boundary priorities 1 and 8, not mid-range values
verification.assertions: parseKey(buildKey(e)) deep-equals the original components for every matrix row; a wrong-segment-count key yields a typed failure

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — The write uses the AWS SDK v3 default credential chain (no hardcoded profile) and is isolated in a single put-event.ts module, so the persist boundary can be swapped in one file.

verification.definingInputProperty: Every source file except the designated persist module
verification.assertions: No AWS SDK import outside put-event.ts; no hardcoded credentials or profile literal anywhere

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — Same-key re-push is a no-op, not an overwrite and not a crash. The write is a conditional put (IfNoneMatch: "*"); an existing key yields PutOutcome { _tag: "AlreadyExists" } and the CLI exits 0 reporting that no write occurred. This preserves the append-only history guarantee in system.md — an event already recorded is never silently replaced.

verification.definingInputProperty: The identical event pushed twice against a real S3 bucket
verification.assertions: First push reports Created and exits 0; second reports AlreadyExists and exits 0; the object's LastModified and ETag are unchanged between the two

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — --dry-run prints the resolved key and the full event body to stdout, performs zero network calls, and exits 0.

verification.definingInputProperty: A dry-run invocation with an unreachable bucket name
verification.assertions: Exit 0; stdout contains both the key and the full event body; no S3Client is constructed and zero requests are issued

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-09 — Bucket identity resolves in the documented precedence order --bucket > EVENT_BUCKET environment variable, and when resolution fails the error names both sources that were tried.

verification.definingInputProperty: Both --bucket and EVENT_BUCKET set to different values, and a case with neither set
verification.assertions: --bucket wins when both present; with neither, the error text names both --bucket and EVENT_BUCKET

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-10 — Failure modes — each produces a specific, actionable stderr message and a documented NON-ZERO exit code, distinct enough for a script to branch on usage errors versus write failures: --type not one of alert/notification; --priority non-integer or outside 1–8; any required flag missing → exit 2 (usage); --payload path missing, unreadable, or malformed JSON; - requested but stdin empty or invalid JSON; --timestamp not a valid ISO instant → exit 2 (usage); AWS credentials missing, expired, or lacking s3:PutObject → exit 3; bucket does not exist, is unreachable, or returns access-denied → exit 4; bucket identity unresolvable → exit 2. Exit codes are documented in the package README.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete enumerated set of 13 failure cases, each with the property that triggers its specific mode
verification.assertions: Each case exits with its exact documented code (2/3/4) and emits a message naming the specific problem; a guard asserts the table length equals 13 so the inventory cannot silently shrink
The exit-code table is documented as the criterion requires

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-11 — Guidance conformance: G-C-P separation (argv/stdin/env gather → pure buildEvent + key compute → putEvent persist), module SRP, Either for pure fallible code and Effect for effectful code per CLAUDE.md, no enums, no accumulator loops, Record lookups over if/else if chains. Verified by biome + typecheck.

verification.command: pnpm --filter @personal-events/s3-repository exec biome check src && pnpm --filter @personal-events/s3-repository typecheck

verification.assertions: No TypeScript enum is used — a counterexample check biome alone does not enforce

tests.productionWriteApproval: GRANTED by the user on 2026-08-31, as specified and without modification. No other object may be read, modified, or removed. Anything beyond this scope requires a fresh approval.
